title: The Lesson Hidden in a Wrong Question
title_ja: 誤った問いに隠された学び
fact_notes: オリジナル論説・架空事例。実在の政策、医療助言、教育効果、調査結果ではない。台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: Students are often asked to provide correct answers to questions that have already been prepared by a teacher.
sentences.ja: 生徒は教師がすでに準備した問いに正答を出すよう求められることが多い。

sentences.en: This arrangement can be useful when the questions are designed to reveal particular aspects of the students' understanding.
sentences.ja: 問いが生徒の理解の特定側面を明らかにするよう設計されているとき、この仕組みは有用になり得る。

sentences.en: However, the questions that learners formulate for themselves can also provide important information about the way they understand a subject.
sentences.ja: しかし学習者自身が作る問いも、科目をどう理解しているかについて重要な情報を提供し得る。

sentences.en: An inaccurate question may reveal a misunderstanding that would remain hidden if the student's work were assessed only through answers to familiar exercises.
sentences.ja: 不正確な問いは身近な練習の解答だけで評価されるなら隠れたままの誤解を示すことがある。

sentences.en: Consider a language class in which students read a passage comparing two imaginary community projects.
sentences.ja: 二つの仮想地域活動を比較する本文を生徒が読む語学授業を考えよう。

sentences.en: One student asks why the author believes that the first project is better than the second.
sentences.ja: ある生徒は作者が第一の活動を第二より優れていると考える理由を尋ねる。

sentences.en: The teacher notices that the passage describes different advantages of the projects without presenting an overall judgment about which one should be selected.
sentences.ja: 教師は本文がどちらを選ぶべきか総合判断を示さず、それぞれの利点を記述すると気づく。

sentences.en: The student's question contains an assumption that is not supported by the text.
sentences.ja: その生徒の問いは本文に支持されない前提を含む。

sentences.en: Instead of providing an immediate answer, the teacher asks the class to identify the statement that would justify the assumption in the original question.
sentences.ja: 即答するのでなく、教師は元の問いの前提を正当化する記述を特定するようクラスに求める。

sentences.en: The students discover that they can identify evidence about the advantages of each project but cannot identify a statement declaring one project superior in every respect.
sentences.ja: 各活動の利点について証拠を特定できるが、一方があらゆる点で優れていると宣言する記述を特定できないと気づく。

sentences.en: They revise the question to ask which conditions might make each project appropriate for a particular community.
sentences.ja: 各活動が特定地域に適する条件は何かを問うよう質問を修正する。

sentences.en: The revised question encourages them to examine the author's comparison without introducing an unsupported conclusion.
sentences.ja: 修正された問いは根拠のない結論を導入せず作者の比較を調べるよう促す。

sentences.en: The teacher also invites the students to explain why the first question was difficult to answer accurately.
sentences.ja: 教師は最初の問いに正確に答えるのが難しかった理由も説明するよう促す。

sentences.en: They recognize that the difficulty involved the structure of the question rather than merely the amount of information they remembered from the passage.
sentences.ja: 困難は本文から覚えた情報量だけでなく問いの構造に関わったと認識する。

sentences.en: This fictional exercise illustrates a possible use of student-generated questions, not a verified method for improving performance in every classroom.
sentences.ja: 架空活動は生徒が作る問いの可能な活用法を例示し、全教室で成績を改善する実証済み方法ではない。

sentences.en: The activity gives the learners a reason to examine the assumptions that shape their reading.
sentences.ja: 活動は読解を形作る前提を調べる理由を学習者に与える。

sentences.en: A question can direct attention toward particular information while making other possibilities less apparent.
sentences.ja: 問いは特定情報に注意を向ける一方で他の可能性を目立たなくし得る。

sentences.en: Learning to formulate a more accurate question can therefore be an important part of learning to interpret information.
sentences.ja: より正確な問いを作ることを学ぶのは情報解釈を学ぶ重要部分になり得る。

sentences.en: The ability to recognize an unsupported assumption is useful even when a learner already knows the literal meaning of every sentence.
sentences.ja: 根拠のない前提を認識する能力は全ての文の文字通りの意味を既に知っていても有用だ。

sentences.en: Sometimes the most valuable lesson begins with a question that cannot be answered as it was originally expressed.
sentences.ja: 時に最も価値ある授業は当初表現されたままでは答えられない問いから始まる。

vocabulary.definition: relating to the basic meaning of words

questions.prompt: Why might student-generated questions be useful?
options: They necessarily replace all teacher-prepared tasks.
They always demonstrate correct understanding.
They remove the need to read a passage.
They can reveal assumptions and misunderstandings.
Both projects are exactly identical.
The author considers the first project better.
The author refuses to describe any advantages.
The second project does not exist.
questions.explanation_ja: 第一が優れているという前提。

options: The passage clearly rejects the first project.
No comparison appears in the passage.
The text offers advantages without an overall preference.
The teacher has already selected the first project.

questions.prompt: What does the teacher ask the students to identify?
options: A statement that would justify the question's assumption.
All unfamiliar words in the passage.
A new community project.
A correct answer from another textbook.

questions.prompt: How does the revised question change the task?
options: It requires choosing the first project immediately.
It eliminates all comparison.
It asks only when the passage was written.
It asks about suitability under different conditions rather than assuming one winner.

questions.prompt: What do the students recognize about the difficulty?
options: It is caused solely by unfamiliar words.
It concerns the question's structure as well as their recall.
It proves the author has made a factual error.
It is unrelated to the question itself.

questions.prompt: What is the scope of the fictional exercise?
options: It illustrates one possible teaching activity without proving its effectiveness.
It demonstrates a method guaranteed to improve every classroom.
It reports measured results from real students.
It establishes that all student questions are inaccurate.

questions.prompt: How can a question affect reading?
options: It always guarantees a correct interpretation.
It changes the literal text.
It directs attention toward some information and away from other possibilities.
It determines the author's private intentions.
Describe without any reason.
Give sufficient reasons for something.
Make something more complicated.
Remove all supporting information.
Correct answers are the only evidence of understanding.
Questions should be answered without examining their premises.
Every inaccurate question has no educational value.
Examining and revising questions can help learners identify assumptions shaping their interpretation.

grammar.focus: Instead of providing an immediate answer

paraphrases.source: An inaccurate question may reveal a misunderstanding that would remain hidden if the student's work were assessed only through answers to familiar exercises.
paraphrases.rewrite: A learner's question may reveal an otherwise unnoticed misunderstanding.

paraphrases.source: The teacher notices that the passage describes different advantages of the projects without presenting an overall judgment about which one should be selected.
paraphrases.rewrite: The text compares advantages but does not choose an overall winner.

paraphrases.source: Instead of providing an immediate answer, the teacher asks the class to identify the statement that would justify the assumption in the original question.
paraphrases.rewrite: The teacher asks for evidence rather than immediately answering.

paraphrases.source: Sometimes the most valuable lesson begins with a question that cannot be answered as it was originally expressed.
paraphrases.rewrite: A question may need revision before a useful answer becomes possible.
